intro:
Use it with an assistant's answer to show the pages the answer was written from, and which claim rests on which page.

It stays out of the answer's way. Once the search is done it is one line above the answer, "Read 5 sources", which opens into a list. The line begins with a bar for each page, as tall as the number of times the answer cites it, so you can see at a glance whether the answer leans on one page or several.

While the search runs, set `status="searching"` and pass the `query`. The list is open, the pages arrive in it one by one, and those still to come hold their place. Set `status="done"` when the list is final and it folds back to its line.

`Sources.Citation` goes in the answer after a claim. Wrap the claim in it, and pointing at the number lights the claim, its bar and its page, and opens a card of what the page says. Pointing at a page in the list lights every claim that rests on it. The answer has to sit inside `Sources` for its citations to find their pages.
usage:
{pages.map((page) => ( ))}

Most often it is under-proofing, which{' '} leaves a tight, gummy middle.

parts.Trigger: The line: a bar for each page, then "Searching …" or "Read 5 sources", then a chevron. A bar is a dot until its page is read, and then grows with each citation of it. A page that could not be read is an empty bar. Pressing the line opens and folds the list once the search is done.
parts.Content: The list of pages, numbered by their place from 1. While searching, it is open, and it holds a place for each page still to come, up to `total`.
parts.Source: One page: its number, its `title`, its site and a line of what it says, the `snippet`. It opens `href` in a new tab. Dots at its end count how many times the answer cites it. `unreachable` keeps a page that could not be opened in the list, marked as such.
parts.Citation: The number of a page, set after a claim in the answer. Give it the claim as children to tie the two together: pointing at either lights both. Pointing at the number also opens a card with the page's title, its snippet and how many claims it backs. Pressing it opens the page.

examples.title: The list open
examples.description: `defaultOpen` starts with the list open. Point at a page and the claims it backs light up in the answer. The first page is cited twice, so its bar is the tallest and it has two dots.

examples.title: Numbers on their own
examples.description: A `Sources.Citation` with no children is just the number. Use it where a claim is the whole sentence, or where several pages back the same words.

examples.title: A page that could not be opened
examples.description: `unreachable` keeps the page in the list, marked, with an empty bar. A reader can tell an answer drawn from two pages apart from a search where one of three failed.

examples.title: In a message
examples.description: Inside a [Message](/docs/web/components/message), `Sources` goes in the answer's content and wraps the bubble, so the line sits above the text it cites.

notes:
### Where the pages come from

With the AI SDK, the pages are the `source-url` parts of an assistant message: `part.url` is the `href` and `part.title` the `title`. Remove duplicates by URL first, because a model can cite the same page twice. A page with no title falls back to its host.

### Numbers

A source is numbered by its place in `Sources.Content`. Pass `index` to number it yourself, for example when the model's citations already carry numbers.

### Accessibility

The line is a button with `aria-expanded`. Each source is a link that says it opens in a new tab and how many times it is cited. Each citation is named "Source 2: its title", and its card opens on focus as well as on hover.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, the searching line does not shimmer, and the bars and the list change without moving.
